successors.note: The infobox ends the culture in -800 ('no burials with these features after 800 BCE', the Italian mission); the Gandhara janapada (sa-01-a) begins in -600, so -799..-601 is a gap on these dates.

correction.text: graves 'spread mainly in the middle Swat River valley' and 'expanded to the valleys of Dir, Kunar, Chitral, and Peshawar', with Buner and Malakand and sites at Taxila and Charsadda (Gandhara region, Swat 100 km, a 60 km disc on Chitral); the page gives no date for the expansion, so the whole range is drawn from -1200

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). Infobox 'c. 1200-800 BCE'; 'Close to the end of the second millennium BCE, large graveyards appear in northern Gandhara'. The page gives no area; the shape resolves to about 73,000 km2. Its core is the middle Swat valley; the Peshawar, Dir, Kunar and Chitral valleys are the page's later expansion (undated).

ledger.note: c. 1200 BCE: large graveyards appear in northern Gandhara. Infobox 'c. 1200-800 BCE', type site 'Swat Protohistoric Graveyards Complex', inhumation phase '(c. 1200-900 BCE)' with 'iron technology' introduced. The year is the infobox's; the page's dates of earlier Swat periods (Ghalegay IV c. 1700-1400, V c. 1400-1000) and the 'admixture between 1900 and 1500 BCE' are not drawn.

region.text: graves 'spread mainly in the middle Swat River valley' and 'expanded to the valleys of Dir, Kunar, Chitral, and Peshawar', with Buner and Malakand and sites at Taxila and Charsadda (Gandhara region, Swat 100 km, a 60 km disc on Chitral); the page gives no date for the expansion, so the whole range is drawn from -1200

ledger.note: c. 800 BCE: the graveyard culture ends. The Italian mission 'holds that there are no burials with these features after 800 BCE'; the Pakistani view is that the graves 'continued in existence from the 8th century BCE until the historic period'. The Gandhara janapada (-600) is the later state of the same valleys.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture known from graveyards at about a dozen named sites; the valleys are the page's, the edges are not.

sources.title: Gandhara grave culture
sources.note: Infobox 1200-800 BCE, the Swat core, the expansion to Dir, Kunar, Chitral and Peshawar, site list, the two views on the end, relations with the Harappan, Indo-Aryan and BMAC hypotheses.

notes: Type culture; no Cliopatria row; no area on the page. The infobox gives 1200-800 but the body also dates the Swat phases to Ghalegay IV (c. 1700-1400) and V (c. 1400-1000) and an admixture 'sometime between 1900 and 1500 BCE', and the Pakistani view runs the graves on to the historic period; the infobox dates are drawn and the rest is soft. The shape is wider than the middle Swat valley because the page lists Charsadda, Taxila and Timargarha and the expansion to Dir, Kunar, Chitral and Peshawar without dating it; a gap-filler should narrow the first decades to the Swat valley if a source dates the spread. Chitral, Buner, Malakand and Dir are not gazetteer places (a 60 km disc at 71.8E 35.85N stands in for Chitral).
